summary: Leading AI experts and tech CEOs, including Sam Altman and Geoffrey Hinton, have issued a warning that AI poses a 'risk of extinction' comparable to pandemics and nuclear war, urging global action. The statement follows an earlier open letter calling for a pause on AI development, and comes amid growing concerns about the technology's societal impacts.

claims.text: AI poses a 'risk of extinction' that should be a global priority alongside pandemics and nuclear war.
claims.evidence_quote: Mitigating the risk of extinction from AI should be a global priority alongside other societal scale risks such as pandemics and nuclear war.

claims.text: The statement was released by the Center for AI Safety on Tuesday.
claims.evidence_quote: a brief statement released by the Center for AI Safety, a San Francisco-based research and advocacy group, on Tuesday.

claims.text: Signatories include Sam Altman, Geoffrey Hinton, Audrey Tang, Sam Harris, and Grimes.
claims.evidence_quote: The signatories include technology experts such as Sam Altman, chief executive of OpenAI, Geoffrey Hinton, known as the 'godfather of AI', and Audrey Tang, Taiwan's digital minister, as well as other notable figures including the neuroscientist Sam Harris and the musician Grimes.

claims.text: An earlier open letter in March, signed by Elon Musk and others, called for a six-month pause on AI development more advanced than GPT-4.
claims.evidence_quote: The warning follows an open letter signed by Elon Musk and other high-profile figures in March that called for a six-month pause on the development of AI more advanced than OpenAI's GPT-4.

claims.text: The open letter said powerful AI systems should be developed only when their effects are positive and risks manageable.
claims.evidence_quote: Powerful AI systems should be developed only once we are confident that their effects will be positive and their risks will be manageable.

claims.text: Concerns about AI include mass job losses, copyright infringement, misinformation, and political instability.
claims.evidence_quote: The rapid advancement of AI has raised concerns about potential negative consequences for society ranging from mass job losses and copyright infringement to the spread of misinformation and political instability.

claims.text: Microsoft researchers said GPT-4 showed 'sparks of AGI' and could solve novel tasks across many domains.
claims.evidence_quote: researchers at Microsoft in March said that GPT-4 showed 'sparks of AGI' and was capable of solving 'novel and difficult tasks that span mathematics, coding, vision, medicine, law, psychology and more, without needing any special prompting'.

claims.text: Geoffrey Hinton quit his job at Google to advocate about AI risks.
claims.evidence_quote: Last month, Hinton, a renowned computer scientist, quit his job at Google so he could spend more time advocating about the risks of AI.

claims.text: Sam Altman called on US Congress to develop AI regulations and recommended a licensing-based approach.
claims.evidence_quote: In an appearance before the United States Congress earlier this month, Altman called on legislators to quickly develop regulations for AI technology and recommended a licensing-based approach.

claims.text: The European Union hopes to pass AI legislation by the end of the year, classifying AI into four risk categories.
claims.evidence_quote: The European Union has said it hopes to pass legislation by the end of the year that would classify AI into four risk-based categories.

claims.text: China has passed legislation governing deep fakes and requires companies to register algorithms.
claims.evidence_quote: China has also taken steps to regulate AI, passing legislation governing deep fakes and requiring companies to register their algorithms with regulators.

claims.text: China proposed strict rules requiring approval before releasing generative AI and restricting politically-sensitive content.
claims.evidence_quote: Beijing has also proposed strict rules to restrict politically-sensitive content and require developers to receive approval before releasing generative AI-based tech.
